ModifyBlockMultiplicative.issue: The sim replaces C#'s HISTORY QUERY with hand-rolled per-power state, and the two disagree about when the allowance resets. C# counts, on every call, History.Entries.OfType<BlockGainedEntry>() where e.HappenedThisTurn(base.CombatState) && e.Actor == target && e.Props.IsCardOrMonsterMove() && e.CardPlay != cardPlay (UnmovablePower.cs:35) -- so the window is the game's own turn window and the exclusion is 'gains from THIS card play do not count against it'. The sim keeps self._plays_used and self._active_card and resets them from on_player_turn_start (powers.py:1127-1130), which is player.py:169. Two divergences follow. (a) THE RESET SLOT: the sim's counter survives the whole enemy turn and is cleared only at the player's next turn start, while C#'s HappenedThisTurn window is the CombatState's, so any block the owner gains during the ENEMY turn from a card or move -- a turn-end auto-play under power/stampede, an on_enemy_turn effect -- lands in a different window on the two sides. (b) THE per-CardPlay EXCLUSION: C# compares CardPlay identities so a card played twice (Duplication, Throwing Axe) counts as TWO plays against the allowance, where the sim compares CARD identity (powers.py:1113) and its on_card_played bump fires once per card (combat.py:514, outside the play loop), so a doubled block card consumes ONE stack in the sim and two in the game -- hook_dispatch's G4 again, not re-verdicted, but here it means a doubled Iron Wave gets DOUBLE block twice in the sim and once in the game. Reachable: Unmovable is a ported Ironclad card (cards/unmovable.py:36) and Throwing Axe is a ported relic from the ported Tanx shrine.

guards.rationale: C# refuses to double a MONSTER's block outright, where powers.py:1111 only tests `target is not self.owner`. Equivalent for the ported content and checked rather than assumed: the sole applier is the Ironclad card (cards/unmovable.py:36, target = ctx.player), no ported monster applies it, and no ported effect copies a player power onto a monster. Named trigger: applying Unmovable to a monster, at which point the sim would double its block and the game would not.

The sim gets this from BlockCmd.apply, whose cmds.py:145 gate (is_powered_attack(props) -- Move and not Unpowered) is the only route to the block-multiplier hooks at all. So unpowered block (power/plating, power/toric_toughness, Rage, block potions) is not doubled on either side, which the sim's docstring states (powers.py:1087-1088). NOTE C#'s predicate admits monster-MOVE block as well as card block; that arm is unreachable here because the owner is always the player and a monster move never grants the player block.
powers.py:1111 `card is None -> 1.0` plus the owner test. Single-player tautology for the ownership half.
